To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

T cell apoptosis and transplant‐related atherosclerosis is associated with increased expression of CD95 ligand, and increased levels of sCD95 and soluble tumour necrosis factors receptors type 1 in the sera of patients with heart transplantation.

(1) CD3+CD4+ T lymphocytes undergo apoptosis in the presence of the allograft; (2) the allograft induces a pronounced susceptibility of T cells to undergo activation‐induced apoptosis; and (3) the allogeneic graft is a potent inducer of apoptosis in T lymphocytes.

the allografted heart may induce a pronounced sensitivity of CD4+ lymphocytes to undergo apoptosis and that antibody‐driven apoptosis‐induced cell may play a significant role in the pathophysiology of TACAD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lymphocyte death pathways in heart transplantation.
the mechanisms of T cell apoptosis in patients with TACAD.
the specific role of lymphocytes in the pathogenesis of TACAD and the possible involvement of apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TACAD patients have a more pronounced susceptibility of CD3+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes to undergo apoptosis and that the TACD is associated with an increased activation of the complement system and a more prominent activation of the coagulation cascade.
the TACAD patients have an activated immune system with increased apoptotic pathways, which is not restricted to T cell subsets.
the increased expression of CD95, CD45RO, sCD95L, IL‐10, sTNFR1 and histones may reflect the activation of T cell‐mediated immunity in heart transplant recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune response in patients with TACAD is characterized by the activation of CD4+ memory cells and the induction of CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) via the Fas/Fas ligand pathway.
the heart allograft induces a pronounced susceptibility of lymphocytes to undergo apoptosis and that the allografted heart is a source of apoptotic material.
the allogeneic graft induces an increased susceptibility of CD4 T cells to undergo activation‐induced apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is a key player in the pathogenesis of heart transplant vasculopathies.
the immune system of the patient is not able to discriminate between a self‐antigen and the allograft.
the activation of CD95‐dependent pathways may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of transplant‐associated coronary disease.
